doc.title: Curtis Fuller — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Claude Black calls him up; Detroit trombonists Rosolino and Murgy
summary: Claude Black heard Fuller in the school music room and invited him to play with the band; Fuller admired Frank Rosolino and his classmate Fred Murgy.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Hearing him on the plane with that band. He heard me playing in the music room when he came in there to check the guys out. He said, “Could you handle it if I call you up to play tonight?” I said, “I’ll try it.” Of course, the school kids where I went said, “Oh god, no, not that guy. Get him out of here, we played for the band.” You know, that’s where I got this movement from (scats a melody). He was almost like Tommy Turk. He was a very good player; he was way ahead of his time. He was playing more musically than Donald Byrd on trumpet. He was the piano player, but Roland Hanna, mister piano, was there. He didn’t even sit at the piano in-between sets. He’d take me aside and he’d say “do you know this song?” He was a little kid himself. I was enamored with him. He was another guy I liked. Frank Rosolino, but equally Fred Murgy, my classmate, I thought he was a tremendous trombonist. He played as well as Frank Rosolino. They can have every trophy out there they want for Frank Rosolino…
Now we are talking Detroit trombone players.
